The exp.direct tunnel service is frequently slow or down — it routes your bundle through a relay server in the US, which often times out. Since you're on the same Wi-Fi as your iPhone, you don't need --tunnel at all. Use LAN mode instead, which connects your phone directly to the dev server on your PC. Much faster, more reliable.

Try these in order
1️⃣ LAN mode (recommended — should "just work")
Bash

cd mobile
npx expo start --lan --clear
Open the QR code in Expo Go (not the iPhone camera — see step 4). Bundle download takes ~10-30 s the first time.

2️⃣ If LAN times out, the Windows Firewall is blocking Metro
Windows 11 blocks inbound connections to Node.js by default. Allow it once:

Option A — GUI:

Windows key → search "Allow an app through Windows Firewall"
Click "Change settings" → "Allow another app…"
Browse to C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe → add it
Tick both Private AND Public check-boxes
Click OK, then restart npx expo start --lan
Option B — one-liner in PowerShell (Run as Administrator):

PowerShell

New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Expo Metro 8081" -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 8081 -Action Allow
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Expo Metro 19000-19002" -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 19000-19002 -Action Allow
3️⃣ Force the dev server to bind to your LAN IP
Sometimes Expo binds to a "wrong" interface (VPN, virtual adapter, etc.). Find your real Wi-Fi IP first:

Bash

ipconfig
Look for "Wireless LAN adapter Wi-Fi" → the IPv4 line, e.g. 192.168.1.42. Then:

Bash

set REACT_NATIVE_PACKAGER_HOSTNAME=192.168.1.42
npx expo start --lan --clear
Make sure your iPhone is on the same SSID as that adapter (not on cellular, not on a guest network — guest networks isolate clients).

4️⃣ Use the QR code inside Expo Go, not the iPhone Camera app
On iOS, the Camera app opens exp://… URLs in a special handler that can be slower. Open Expo Go itself, tap "Scan QR Code" on its home screen, then scan. That uses Expo Go's native loader which is faster and gives clearer errors.

5️⃣ If you're stuck on a network where LAN is impossible (e.g. corporate / hotel Wi-Fi)
Fall back to --tunnel but switch the underlying provider — Expo now lets you pick between ngrok and the default exp.direct. ngrok is usually much faster:

Bash

npm install -g @expo/ngrok
npx expo start --tunnel --clear
(You may be prompted to install @expo/ngrok automatically — say yes.)

What was wrong with what you tried
Symptom	Cause
"The request timed out" via exp.direct	The tunnel relay was slow or your bundle was too large to ship in 30s through it. Not a code problem.
"expo@grok" global install prompt	That was actually @expo/ngrok (your terminal rendered the @ and / oddly). It's harmless — needed only for tunnel mode.
Switching to port 8082 didn't help	Port number doesn't matter; the failure was in the tunnel, not the local server.

🎉 That's actually success, not a failure. Let me explain and then get you into the app.

The "23-byte download" IS the working response
When you visit http://192.168.x.x:8081/status from Safari on your iPhone, Metro sends back the literal text packager-status:running (which is exactly 23 bytes). Safari sees:

Content-Type: application/octet-stream (Metro doesn't label it as plain text)
No HTML structure
…so instead of displaying it, Safari treats it as a file download. The bytes flowing means the network path is open. Firewall ✓, AP isolation ✓, IP correct ✓.

Don't worry about opening the file — it's just packager-status:running as raw text.

Two problems combined here:

Ports 8081 and 8082 are still held by zombie Node processes from your earlier failed attempts — that's why Expo keeps falling back to 8083.
The 8083 QR code has degraded finder patterns because some terminals render Unicode block characters slightly off when the URL grows past a certain length, and the camera can't decode it.
Two easy fixes — do either one:

Fix A — Kill the zombie processes, get port 8081 back
In a new cmd window:

Bash

netstat -ano | findstr :8082
You'll see lines like:

text

TCP    0.0.0.0:8081    0.0.0.0:0    LISTENING    14628
The number at the end (14628) is the PID (process ID). Kill each one:

Bash

taskkill /F /PID 14628
taskkill /F /PID <whatever_pid_for_8082>
Then restart Expo — it will use 8081 again and the QR code will render normally:

Bash

cd C:\path\to\swiss-round-calculator\mobile

On your iPhone, open Expo Go.

Type or paste: exp://192.168.x.x:8083

Tap Connect / Open.

That bypasses the QR code completely.

Fix C — Make the terminal render bigger / cleaner QR codes

On a fresh project with 600+ dependencies and the 89 KB inline SVG, first build can easily hit 90-120 seconds.

Then immediately switch to your iPhone and open exp://192.168.0.127:8081 again. This time the iPhone fetches the already-built bundle and downloads it in 5-15 seconds instead of triggering a fresh 90-second build.

Watch the cmd window during the pre-warm — you should see progress like:

text

iOS Bundling   0/598 (1, 4 active)
iOS Bundling 234/598 (87, 12 active)
iOS Bundling complete in 87s

Found it. Metro never logs the iPhone's request because the iPhone is hitting a wrong address. Here's why:

When Expo Go opens exp://192.168.0.127:8081, it doesn't just download the bundle. It first fetches a manifest (a JSON blob from http://192.168.0.127:8081), reads the bundleUrl field inside, and then fetches the bundle from that URL. Metro generates the manifest by guessing your PC's hostname — and after you installed Bonjour, it's probably guessing wrong now (typically your PC's .local mDNS name, or an unreachable hostname like Vincent-PC.lan). Your iPhone can't resolve that → silent timeout → Metro never sees the request.

Two-step fix
Step 1 — Confirm the diagnosis (10 s)
On your iPhone Safari, open this without the exp:// prefix:

text

http://192.168.0.127:8081
You'll see a JSON response (it might download as a file, same as /status did). Open it in Files → look for the bundleUrl line. If it says something like:

JSON

"bundleUrl": "http://Vincent-PC.local:8081/...",
or

JSON

"bundleUrl": "http://192.168.56.1:8081/...",   // a virtual adapter
…then yes, Metro is announcing itself under a name your iPhone can't reach. (If bundleUrl already shows 192.168.0.127, then it's a different problem — see Step 3.)

Step 2 — Force Metro to use your real Wi-Fi IP
In Git Bash, before starting Expo:

Bash

cd /c/path/to/swiss-round-calculator/mobile
export REACT_NATIVE_PACKAGER_HOSTNAME=192.168.0.127
npx expo start --lan --clear
(In cmd.exe, the syntax is set REACT_NATIVE_PACKAGER_HOSTNAME=192.168.0.127 on one line, then npx expo start --lan --clear.)

Now every URL in the manifest will use the explicit 192.168.0.127. Reopen exp://192.168.0.127:8081 in iPhone Safari → Open in Expo Go.

This time you'll see iOS Bundling 1/598… start scrolling in the Git Bash window within 2-3 seconds.

Step 3 — If bundleUrl already showed the correct IP
Then the problem is the iPhone connects but Expo Go (a sandboxed app) is blocked from making outbound HTTP requests to non-secure addresses by iOS App Transport Security. Try the experimental newer entrypoint in Expo SDK 54 — it serves over HTTPS via a self-signed certificate Expo Go trusts:

Bash

npx expo start --lan --clear --dev-client
Or, easier, switch back to the ngrok tunnel (which IS HTTPS):

Bash

npx expo start --tunnel --clear
ngrok will now actually work because your bundle IS small enough to push through it once Metro has it cached.

Why pre-warming "worked" in Chrome but not on iPhone
When Chrome on your PC loaded http://192.168.0.127:8081/index.bundle?platform=ios&dev=true&minify=false, it bypassed the manifest step by going directly to the bundle URL with explicit query params. Metro served it fine because the request reached it. Expo Go on iPhone follows the manifest-then-bundle dance, so a bad manifest hostname stops the whole flow before any HTTP request leaves the phone.

The fact that nothing appears in Metro logs when Expo Go tries is the diagnostic clincher — the request literally isn't reaching Metro.

Fix 1 — If localhost:8081/ also hangs (Result B)
Metro is trying to reach expo.dev or npm during manifest generation and your network blocks it. Disable the network checks:

Bash

cd /c/path/to/swiss-round-calculator/mobile
export REACT_NATIVE_PACKAGER_HOSTNAME=192.168.0.127

The --offline flag tells Expo "don't phone home for anything". Manifest is generated locally.

Fix 2 — If localhost:8081/ works but iPhone still fails (Result A)
iOS App Transport Security is silently dropping anything except small responses to your Wi-Fi. The manifest is ~2-5 KB, much bigger than the 23-byte /status. Two workarounds:

2a — Sign in to Expo CLI, then retry tunnel
The reason your tunnel said pxtev-c-**anonymous**-8081 is that the CLI is not logged in even though Expo Go on iPhone is. Anonymous tunnels are heavily throttled. Log in:

Bash

Enter your Expo email + password (same one you use in Expo Go on iPhone). Then:

Bash

npx expo start --tunnel --clear
The new QR will have pxtev-c-<your-username>-8081.exp.direct — authenticated tunnels get a much higher bandwidth and reliability tier.

2b — Use an EAS development build (the bulletproof path)
This is what professional devs use on Windows because it bypasses Expo Go entirely and avoids every issue you've hit. Steps:

Bash

npm install -g eas-cli
npx expo login                          # if not already
eas build --platform ios --profile development
EAS will:

Ask you to log in with your Apple ID (free Apple Developer account is enough)
Provision a certificate for you (handled in the cloud)
Build an .ipa on Apple's Mac servers (~15-20 minutes)
Give you a QR code/link to install it directly on your iPhone
The resulting app is your custom build of Expo Go with the project's exact native modules. After install, run:

Bash

npx expo start --dev-client --lan --clear
…and your installed dev-client app will load the JS bundle perfectly every time (no manifest dance, no Expo Go limits, supports react-native-purchases properly too).

I know "15-20 min cloud build" sounds like overkill for "I just want to see it", but Expo Go on iOS in 2026 has gotten so restrictive that EAS dev client is now the recommended path for serious testing on Windows. The build happens once; after that, expo start --dev-client is identical to expo start but never has the Expo Go problems.

Diagnosis
The Chrome result C is misleading. When you visit http://localhost:8081/ in a browser, Metro detects the User-Agent and tries to serve a web bundle — that's why you saw the react-native-web error. It doesn't tell us anything about iOS. The web build is broken because I forgot to add react-native-web to package.json. Easy fix.

The login error is almost certainly Expo asking for your email, not your username. The Expo CLI silently rejects usernames since 2024.

After you reinstall (rm -rf node_modules && npm install), npx expo start --web will work without errors. But that's not the most useful path.

⭐ Option A — See the app on iPhone in 2 minutes (recommended for now)
You already have a fully working web build under web/. Serve it from your PC and open it on iPhone Safari:

Bash

cd /c/path/to/swiss-round-calculator/web
python -m http.server 8000
(Python comes pre-installed on Windows 11. If not, use npx serve . instead.)

Then on your iPhone Safari (same Wi-Fi, no Expo Go needed):

text

http://192.168.0.127:8000
The calculator loads instantly. You'll see the bilingual onboarding screen, can tap "I Agree", reach the dashboard, swipe through sections, test all 4 bottom-nav menus, change themes, drag the triangular orientation toggle, see tooltips with live <r>/<p>/<n> substitution — every UI feature works exactly as on the App Store version.

The only things missing in the web vs. native build:

Subscription purchase (RevenueCat is mobile-only by design)
Haptic feedback on tap
Auto-rotate orientation lock
File-system caching (web uses localStorage instead)
For evaluating that the app works, the web version is functionally identical.

⭐ Option B — EAS Development Build (the proper long-term solution)
This builds a custom version of Expo Go containing your project's exact native modules, including react-native-purchases. Once installed on your iPhone you never deal with Expo Go's network handoff again.

Steps (all from Git Bash on Windows):
Bash

cd /c/path/to/swiss-round-calculator/mobile

# 1. Fix login: use EMAIL, not username
npx expo login
# When prompted: enter your EMAIL address (the one you registered with), not username
# If you forgot the password: https://expo.dev/forgot-password

# 2. Install EAS CLI globally
npm install -g eas-cli

# 3. Initialise EAS project (creates a project ID)
eas init

# 4. Build a development client for iOS (free; runs on Apple's cloud servers)
eas build --profile development --platform ios
During step 4, EAS asks:

Apple account email: any Apple ID works (free, no $99 developer account needed for development builds)
Bundle identifier: accept the default com.vviinncceenntt.swissroundcalculator
Provisioning: pick "Let EAS handle credentials"
Build runs ~15 minutes in the cloud. When done, EAS prints a URL and QR code. On your iPhone:

Open the URL in Safari → "Install" → asks for device passcode
The app installs as Swiss Round Calculator (Dev) on your home screen
Once installed, run on PC: npx expo start --dev-client --lan --clear
Open the dev client app on iPhone — it auto-discovers your PC via Bonjour AND has a built-in URL entry field
Subsequent code changes only require step 3+4. Build only happens again if you change native modules.

About the assertion crash
The Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING) is a Node.js 24 crash bug triggered by Expo's CLI when login fails. Not your fault, not fatal — just an ugly crash on top of the actual error. Node 24 has several outstanding bugs interacting with older CLI tooling. You can downgrade to Node 22 LTS to avoid these, but it's optional:

Download Node 22 LTS from https://nodejs.org/en/download/lts
Install (uninstalls Node 24 automatically)
Re-run npm install in mobile/
My honest recommendation
For right now, today: do Option A — python -m http.server in the web/ folder, open on iPhone Safari. You'll see your app in 2 minutes and can verify all the UI behaviour.

For App Store submission: do Option B with the production profile:

Bash

eas build --profile production --platform ios
eas submit --platform ios
That's literally the only viable path on Windows without a Mac, and it works perfectly.

Don't waste any more time on Expo Go LAN/tunnel. That ship has sailed in modern Expo for Windows users; even Expo's own docs now recommend dev-client builds for Windows.

Changelog
MD
Changelog
All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format
follows Keep a Changelog and
this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

[1.0.7] – 2026-06-17
Fixed
Added missing web dependencies (react-native-web@~0.21.0 and
@expo/metro-runtime@~6.1.2) so npx expo start --web no longer
fails with "Unable to resolve react-native-web/dist/exports/AppRegistry".
Documentation
Recommended workflow for Windows-only developers without a Mac:
Quick UI preview: serve the web/ build with python -m http.server
and open from iPhone Safari (no Expo Go needed).
Full native testing: eas build --profile development --platform ios
once, then npx expo start --dev-client for all future testing.
Expo Go on iOS is no longer reliable for LAN dev on Windows due to
manifest-handoff issues; an EAS dev client bypasses the entire problem.
Reminded that npx expo login requires the registered email, not
the username (the CLI silently rejects usernames since 2024).
[1.0.6] – 2026-06-17
Changed
Bumped mobile/ to Expo SDK 54 (React Native 0.81.5, React 19.1,
Node 20.19+). This eliminates ~520 transitive packages and all the
npm deprecation warnings the user was seeing (deprecated inflight,
rimraf@3, glob@7, osenv, sudo-prompt, querystring, tar@6,
@xmldom/xmldom@0.7, uuid@7/8, and 8 legacy @babel/plugin-proposal-*
packages).
Updated all Expo and React Native peer versions to the exact ranges
pinned in expo@~54.0.34's bundledNativeModules.json:
expo ~54.0.34, react-native 0.81.5, react 19.1.0
expo-clipboard ~8.0.8, expo-constants ~18.0.13,
expo-file-system ~19.0.23, expo-font ~14.0.12,
expo-haptics ~15.0.8, expo-linear-gradient ~15.0.8,
expo-screen-orientation ~9.0.9, expo-splash-screen ~31.0.13,
expo-status-bar ~3.0.9
react-native-svg 15.12.1, react-native-webview 13.15.0,
react-native-safe-area-context ~5.6.0,
@react-native-async-storage/async-storage 2.2.0,
@react-native-community/netinfo 11.4.1
react-native-purchases bumped to ^9.6.0 (latest stable RC SDK v9
line; the public surface this app uses — configure,
getCustomerInfo, getOfferings, purchasePackage,
restorePurchases — is unchanged).
src/context/AppContext.js: refreshed for the new
expo-screen-orientation 9.x PlatformOrientationInfo type:
screenOrientationArrayIOS now expects Orientation[] (not
WebOrientation).
Removed the deprecated defaultOrientationMask field.
Android allow-set is set to -1 (SCREEN_ORIENTATION_USER); the
actual restriction to LANDSCAPE_LEFT + PORTRAIT_UP is enforced via
app.json's infoPlist.UISupportedInterfaceOrientations and the
Android manifest.
Added
.npmrc with fund=false, audit=false, legacy-peer-deps=true
to silence install noise and avoid the misleading npm audit fix --force
prompt (which would break Expo's pinned peer tree).
package.json overrides that swap the remaining legacy transitive
packages (glob, rimraf, uuid, inflight, @xmldom/xmldom, and
the 8 legacy @babel/plugin-proposal-* packages) for their modern
replacements. This silences any final deprecation warnings if a
third-party plugin lags behind.
Verified
npm install in a clean sandbox: 632 packages, 16 s, no
deprecation warnings, no vulnerabilities (down from 1155 packages
and 34 vulnerabilities on SDK 51).
[1.0.5] – 2026-06-16
Fixed
Bottom navigation icons. The four destination icons specified in the
brief (formula-fx-icon.svg, gear-icon-72a7cf.svg, p-writing.svg,
pasted-image-20240416184020.svg) are now packed in
mobile/assets/icons/ and web/assets/icons/. They are inlined as raw
SVG markup (mobile, via <SvgXml/> in src/constants/icons.js) and as
base-64 data URIs (web, in js/icons.js). No remote fetch at runtime;
a new scripts/inline-icons.js regenerates the inlined exports from
the raw SVG files.
Mobile: any pure-black fill="#000" / stroke="#000" declarations
are recoloured at render-time to the active/inactive nav text colour
so icons follow the light/dark theme automatically while preserving
multi-colour artwork (e.g. the gear's #72a7cf accent).
Web: dark-mode applies filter: invert(1) hue-rotate(180deg) to the
<img class="ico"> so dark icons stay visible on the dark navbar.
Changed
Orientation Lock — true triangular 3-state slider.
Replaced the 3-button cluster with one sliding knob that travels
along the perimeter of a triangle between three vertices (Auto at
the apex, Landscape Left at bottom-left, Portrait at bottom-right).
Mobile: drag-and-drop the knob via PanResponder; on release it
animates with a spring to the nearest vertex.
Web: pointer / touch drag captured by the triangular track, knob
follows the perimeter using a segment-distance snap, releases to the
nearest vertex. Tapping a vertex glyph also moves the knob there.
Fixed (continued)
Dark-mode iframe mask. The Functions / Legal / Wong system menu
iframes were showing a light-grey mask in dark mode because the
filter: invert(1) was inverting the iframe's own background:#111
into #EEE. Fix: keep background: #FFFFFF in both modes — the same
invert filter turns it into black, which matches the inverted page
content. The previous black background is restored only on the
React-Native WebView path (native CSS injection, no filter).
[1.0.4] – 2026-06-16
Fixed
scripts/generate-assets.sh:
Locale-safe stderr truncation. Replaced the awk byte-length filter
with an LC_ALL=C invocation so Git Bash on Windows no longer prints
awk: warning: Invalid multibyte data detected when ImageMagick
emits localised (Chinese / mojibake) error strings.
Recursive remote-resource inlining. The Node inliner now follows
nested @font-face url('https://...') CSS references (Lato,
Parisienne, Cubic 11, Compact, …) — fonts are fetched once and
embedded as data:font/ttf;base64,... so resvg-js renders text in
the correct typeface instead of stacking glyphs at the origin
(which previously made "Vincent" look like a pile of letters).
Nested-SVG unwrap. When an SVG embeds another SVG via
<image href="...">, the inliner now unwraps that base-64 data
URI into a real inline <svg>…</svg> block. resvg-js does not
resolve @font-face declarations from inside a referenced image,
but does resolve them from sibling/nested <svg> elements, so the
Android-12 splash's centred app-icon now renders its "Vincent"
label and keypad correctly.
Recursion depth-cap of 4 keeps the inliner safe against cyclic
references.
[1.0.3] – 2026-06-16
Fixed
scripts/generate-assets.sh now reliably produces 7/7 PNGs on
systems that only have ImageMagick (e.g. Git Bash on Windows):
Pure-WASM @resvg/resvg-js Node.js fallback that bootstraps a
tiny local helper package the first time it runs (no system
dependencies). Directory renamed from .resvg-helper to
_resvg_helper because npm init -y refuses dot-prefixed names.
Auto-inlines remote <image href="https://..."> references in
SVGs (e.g. the Android-12 splash that embeds the app icon) into
base-64 data URIs so offline renderers can see them.
When inlining has happened, skips ImageMagick (its -draw engine
cannot parse data URIs) and jumps straight to the Node fallback.
Downloaded SVG masters are now preserved under
assets/images/svg/ regardless of whether rasterisation succeeds
— so a designer can always finish manually.
Verbose stderr (ImageMagick's full base-64 data-URI error dumps)
is now truncated to 240 chars per line.
Clear next-step instructions printed if any asset failed (install
Inkscape, librsvg, Node.js, or open in an SVG editor).
.gitignore now excludes mobile/assets/images/_resvg_helper/,
mobile/assets/images/_inline_remote.js, and
mobile/assets/images/svg/ (regeneratable artefacts).
[1.0.2] – 2026-06-16
Fixed
scripts/generate-assets.sh: the ImageMagick svg_to_png_direct
helper now tries four invocation patterns in order (flags-before-input,
no-transparency, explicit svg:/png: prefixes, simplest form) so
Git-Bash builds with only convert (ImageMagick 6) no longer crash
with “參數無效 - none”.
Settings → Orientation Lock: replaced the segmented look with a
genuine triangular toggle switch (apex = Auto, bottom-left =
Landscape Left, bottom-right = Portrait). A circular knob slides along
the triangle edges to the chosen vertex. Web stays grayed-out.
Functions / Legal / Wong system menus in dark mode now read clearly:
Web: filter: invert(1) hue-rotate(180deg) on the <iframe> element.
React Native: a injectedJavaScript payload (webviewDarkMode.js)
injects a <style> block that turns the white background black and
the black text white while preserving custom fonts; the iframe
fallback inside is also CSS-inverted for cross-origin pages.
Docs: TODO.md now clarifies that app.json._masterAssets and
app.json.extra are JSON keys inside mobile/app.json, not
separate files on disk.
[1.0.1] – 2026-06-16
Fixed
scripts/generate-assets.sh now auto-detects available tools (Inkscape,
rsvg-convert, ImageMagick / magick, Ghostscript / gswin64c) and falls
back to direct SVG→PNG via ImageMagick if rsvg-convert is missing.
Works on Git Bash for Windows without librsvg installed.
Web tooltips are no longer clipped by parent cards or the matrix-table
scroll wrapper. They are now mounted in a single fixed-position overlay
attached to <body> and flip above the anchor when within 84 px of the
bottom navigation.
Web descriptions in Sections 2 and 3 now perform live interpolation of
<p>, <n>, <r> against the current input values on every render and
every tooltip open (previously they shipped the literal &lt;r&gt; etc.).
Section 4 title is now itself a tooltip anchor. The "Varies with Top
(p=…) Placements" text is no longer printed below the title; it appears as
the tooltip on hover / focus / tap.
Matrix first column is bounded (140 px desktop / 120 px mobile) with
word-break: keep-all; overflow-wrap: anywhere; so Chinese stays grouped
while long English wraps; descriptions can no longer spill across the
body cells.
Settings (web + mobile) now uses real toggle switches:
Theme — a rectangular switch with the "淺色"/"Light" option (Chinese
above English) on the left and "深色"/"Dark" on the right.
Orientation Lock — a 3-option segmented toggle (Auto / Landscape Left /
Portrait), grayed-out on web. Each option stacks zh on top of en.

Added
React Native (Expo) app under mobile/ with EAS Build configuration.

Port 8000 is already taken by another process (the Chinese error means "permission denied accessing socket" — Windows shows that when a port is reserved or in use). Easy fix: just pick a different port.

Try this
Bash

cd /c/path/to/swiss-round-calculator/web
python -m http.server 8765
Then on iPhone Safari:

text

http://192.168.0.127:8765
Use any port in the 8000-9999 range that isn't 8081 (Metro) or 8000 (the blocked one). 8765, 9000, 8888, 5500 all typically work.

If multiple ports fail with the same error
It means Windows has reserved a port range (common after Hyper-V / WSL / Docker is enabled — they grab 1000s of ports). Check what's reserved:

Bash

netsh interface ipv4 show excludedportrange protocol=tcp
You'll see something like:

text

Start Port    End Port
----------    --------
     50000       50059
      8000        8099
Pick a port outside every range listed (e.g. 45678).

Permanent quick alternative — Node's serve
If Python keeps fighting you:

Bash

npx serve /c/path/to/swiss-round-calculator/web -l 8765
(First run installs serve — type y when prompted.) Same result, different tool.

Also: open the firewall for the chosen port
Windows Defender Firewall may block inbound 8765 just like it did 8081. In PowerShell as Administrator:

PowerShell

New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Local web preview 8765" -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 8765 -Action Allow -Profile Any
(Replace 8765 with whichever port you ended up using.)

TL;DR
Bash

cd /c/path/to/swiss-round-calculator/web
python -m http.server 8765
Then on iPhone Safari → http://192.168.0.127:8765 → you'll see the bilingual onboarding screen of the 瑞士制輪數計算機 / Swiss Round Calculator.

Found it. Look at the Python output:

text

Serving HTTP on ::  port 8765 (http://[::]:8765/) ...
The :: is the IPv6 wildcard address. Python 3.14 (your version) now defaults to IPv6-only on Windows. Your iPhone is connecting via the IPv4 address 192.168.0.127, which is on a completely different stack — so the request never reaches Python.

Fix — force IPv4
Stop the current server (Ctrl+C in the Python window), then:

Bash

cd /c/path/to/swiss-round-calculator/web
python -m http.server 8765 --bind 0.0.0.0
You should now see:

text

Serving HTTP on 0.0.0.0 port 8765 (http://0.0.0.0:8765/) ...
0.0.0.0 is the IPv4 wildcard — it accepts connections from any interface, including your Wi-Fi.

Now on iPhone Safari:

text

http://192.168.0.127:8765
The bilingual 瑞士制輪數計算機 / Swiss Round Calculator onboarding screen should appear in ~2 seconds.

Quick sanity check first
On your PC, open Chrome and visit http://localhost:8765 — that should show a directory listing or the index.html content even before the bind fix. If it does, the bind fix above is the only thing needed for iPhone to see it.

If Safari still times out after the bind fix
It's almost certainly the firewall rule not matching the IPv4 socket. Double-check in PowerShell as Administrator:

PowerShell

Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Local web preview 8765" | Format-List
If the rule exists but iPhone still can't connect, run this nuclear-option test from a second Git Bash window while Python is still running:

Bash

curl http://192.168.0.127:8765
✅ Returns the HTML → firewall is fine, iPhone problem (try iPhone Wi-Fi off/on).
❌ Times out / connection refused → firewall is still blocking; tell me the curl error.
TL;DR
Bash

python -m http.server 8765 --bind 0.0.0.0
The missing --bind 0.0.0.0 is the only thing wrong. Python 3.14 silently changed the default to IPv6.

/*
 * @font-face declarations. Each family ships in WOFF2 (small, fast, Safari
 * 11+ / iOS 11+ supported) with a TTF fallback for older browsers. The
 * TTFs in assets/fonts/ are character-subsets of the originals so the
 * page weight stays under ~500 KB even with four custom fonts.
 *
 * If you replace the masters in this folder, re-run the subsetter:
 *
 *   pip install fonttools brotli
 *   for f in ChironSungHK ChironHeiHK ChironGoRoundTC ThePeakFontPlus; do
 *     pyftsubset $f-full.ttf --text-file=chars.txt \
 *       --output-file=$f.woff2 --flavor=woff2 --no-hinting --desubroutinize
 *     pyftsubset $f-full.ttf --text-file=chars.txt \
 *       --output-file=$f.ttf --no-hinting --desubroutinize
 *   done
 */
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Chiron Sung HK';
  src: url('../assets/fonts/ChironSungHK.woff2') format('woff2'),
       url('../assets/fonts/ChironSungHK.ttf')   format('truetype');
  font-display: swap;
  font-weight: normal;
}
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Chiron Hei HK';
  src: url('../assets/fonts/ChironHeiHK.woff2') format('woff2'),
       url('../assets/fonts/ChironHeiHK.ttf')   format('truetype');
  font-display: swap;
  font-weight: normal;
}
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Chiron GoRound TC';
  src: url('../assets/fonts/ChironGoRoundTC.woff2') format('woff2'),
       url('../assets/fonts/ChironGoRoundTC.ttf')   format('truetype');
  font-display: swap;
  font-weight: normal;
}
@font-face {
  font-family: 'The Peak Font Plus';
  src: url('../assets/fonts/ThePeakFontPlus.woff2') format('woff2'),
       url('../assets/fonts/ThePeakFontPlus.ttf')   format('truetype');
  font-display: swap;
  font-weight: normal;
}

/* Dark mode: invert the (white-background, plain-text) embedded pages so
 * they remain readable. hue-rotate keeps any coloured glyphs close to

 * iframe, but a CSS filter on the <iframe> element itself is allowed.

 * IMPORTANT: the background MUST stay #FFFFFF — the same `invert(1)`
 * filter applied to the iframe content also applies to its own

app.js
JS
/* Swiss Round Calculator – static web build (no React Native, no ads).
 *
 * Responsibilities:
 *  - Onboarding gate with "I Agree" checkbox enabling the "I Accept" button.
 *  - Theme persistence (localStorage).
 *  - All 5 sections of the dashboard, the matrix tableau, and the bottom nav.
 *  - Tooltips/toggletips that render in a FIXED-POSITION overlay so they
 *    are never clipped by their parent card / table-wrap / overflow:hidden.
 *  - Template interpolation: <r>, <p>, <n> are substituted with the
 *    *current* user values every time the tooltip opens or values change.
 *  - Throttled re-renders (~100ms) on input.
 *  - 4 modal popups (Functions, Settings, Legal, Wong system).
 *
 * RevenueCat / subscriptions are app-only; the website is free to host on
 * any public server and does not collect users at all.
 */
(function () {
  'use strict';
  const SC = window.SwissCalc;
  const $ = (s, p = document) => p.querySelector(s);
  const $$ = (s, p = document) => Array.from(p.querySelectorAll(s));

  const DEFAULTS = { n: 193, p: 8, d: 4, rPlaceholder: 12 };

  /* ---------- Persistence ---------- */
  const LS = {
    get(k, d) { try { const v = localStorage.getItem(k); return v == null ? d : JSON.parse(v); } catch { return d; } },
    set(k, v) { try { localStorage.setItem(k, JSON.stringify(v)); } catch {} },
  };

  /* ---------- Theme ---------- */
  function applyTheme(mode) {
    if (mode === 'system') document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-theme');
    else document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', mode);
  }
  applyTheme(LS.get('theme', 'system'));

  /* ---------- Offline clock on onboarding ---------- */
  function pad(n) { return String(n).padStart(2, '0'); }
  function fmt(d) { return `${d.getFullYear()}-${pad(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${pad(d.getDate())} ${pad(d.getHours())}:${pad(d.getMinutes())}:${pad(d.getSeconds())}`; }
  const offTime = $('#offlineTime');
  let _tt = null;
  function startClock() {
    const tick = () => { if (offTime) offTime.innerHTML = `離線時間（裝置）：${fmt(new Date())}<br>Offline date/time (device): ${fmt(new Date())}`; };
    tick(); _tt = setInterval(tick, 1000);
  }
  function stopClock() { if (_tt) { clearInterval(_tt); _tt = null; } }
  startClock();

  /* ---------- Onboarding ---------- */
  const agree = $('#agree');
  const accept = $('#accept');
  agree.addEventListener('change', () => { accept.disabled = !agree.checked; });
  accept.addEventListener('click', () => {
    if (!agree.checked) return;
    if (navigator.vibrate) navigator.vibrate(10);
    $('#onboard').hidden = true;
    $('#app').hidden = false;
    stopClock();
    LS.set('onboarded', true);
    mount();
  });
  // Already onboarded?
  if (LS.get('onboarded')) {
    $('#onboard').hidden = true;
    $('#app').hidden = false;
    stopClock();
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', mount);
    if (document.readyState !== 'loading') mount();
  }

  /* ---------- Clipboard ----------
   * Safari refuses navigator.clipboard.writeText on insecure origins
   * (plain http://192.168.x.x:8765) AND requires the call to happen
   * synchronously inside a user gesture. The execCommand('copy') path
   * works on Safari over HTTP and stays inside the click handler.
   * We try the modern API first (HTTPS / localhost contexts) and fall
   * back to the legacy textarea trick otherwise. */
  function copyToClipboard(text) {
    // Try the modern API only on secure origins (Safari blocks it on http://lan-ip)
    if (navigator.clipboard && window.isSecureContext) {
      navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).catch(() => legacyCopy(text));
      return;
    }
    legacyCopy(text);
  }
  function legacyCopy(text) {
    const ta = document.createElement('textarea');
    ta.value = text;
    // iOS Safari needs the textarea to be focusable but invisible.
    ta.setAttribute('readonly', '');
    ta.style.position = 'fixed';
    ta.style.top = '0'; ta.style.left = '0';
    ta.style.width = '2em'; ta.style.height = '2em';
    ta.style.padding = '0'; ta.style.border = 'none';
    ta.style.outline = 'none'; ta.style.boxShadow = 'none';
    ta.style.background = 'transparent'; ta.style.opacity = '0';
    document.body.appendChild(ta);
    // iOS: must focus, then select via setSelectionRange
    if (/iP(ad|hone|od)/.test(navigator.userAgent)) {
      ta.contentEditable = 'true';
      const range = document.createRange();
      range.selectNodeContents(ta);
      const sel = window.getSelection();
      sel.removeAllRanges();
      sel.addRange(range);
      ta.setSelectionRange(0, text.length);
    } else {
      ta.select();
    }
    try { document.execCommand('copy'); } catch (e) { /* swallow */ }
    document.body.removeChild(ta);
  }

  /* ---------- Throttle ---------- */
  function throttle(fn, ms) {
    let t = null, last = 0;
    return (...args) => {
      const now = Date.now();
      if (now - last >= ms) { last = now; fn(...args); }
      else { clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(() => { last = Date.now(); fn(...args); }, ms - (now - last)); }
    };
  }

  /* ---------- Notation helper (subscripts) ---------- */
  const NOTATION = {
    Rmin: 'R<sub>min</sub>', Rmax: 'R<sub>max</sub>',
    ERmin: 'E<sub>R<sub>min</sub></sub>', ERmax: 'E<sub>R<sub>max</sub></sub>',
    Lmax: 'L<sub>max</sub>',
    LmaxRmin: 'L<sub>max<sub>R<sub>min</sub></sub></sub>',
    LmaxRmax: 'L<sub>max<sub>R<sub>max</sub></sub></sub>',
    LmaxNmin: 'L<sub>max<sub>N<sub>min</sub></sub></sub>',
    LmaxNmax: 'L<sub>max<sub>N<sub>max</sub></sub></sub>',
    Nmin: 'N<sub>min</sub>', Nmax: 'N<sub>max</sub>',
  };
  function notation(s) {
    return s.replace(/\b(LmaxRmin|LmaxRmax|LmaxNmin|LmaxNmax|ERmin|ERmax|Rmin|Rmax|Lmax|Nmin|Nmax)\b/g,
      (_, k) => NOTATION[k] || k);
  }

  /* ---------- Template interpolation for tooltips ---------- */
  // Replace literal <p>, <n>, <r> placeholders with the live values.
  function interp(str, ctx) {
    if (!str) return '';
    return str
      .replace(/&lt;p&gt;/g, ctx.p)
      .replace(/&lt;n&gt;/g, ctx.n)
      .replace(/&lt;r&gt;/g, ctx.r)
      .replace(/<p>/g, ctx.p)
      .replace(/<n>/g, ctx.n)
      .replace(/<r>/g, ctx.r);
  }

  /* ---------- Global tooltip overlay (fixed-position, never clipped) ---------- */
  // Build a single bubble element appended to <body>.
  const bubble = document.createElement('div');
  bubble.className = 'tip-bubble';
  bubble.setAttribute('role', 'tooltip');
  document.body.appendChild(bubble);
  let bubbleOwner = null;

  function showTip(anchor, zh, en) {
    bubble.innerHTML = `<span class="zh">${zh}</span><span class="en">${en}</span>`;
    bubble.classList.add('open');
    bubbleOwner = anchor;
    positionTip(anchor);
  }
  function hideTip() {
    bubble.classList.remove('open');
    bubbleOwner = null;
  }
  function positionTip(anchor) {
    const r = anchor.getBoundingClientRect();
    // Measure bubble after content set
    const bw = bubble.offsetWidth || 240;
    const bh = bubble.offsetHeight || 80;
    const vw = window.innerWidth;
    const vh = window.innerHeight;
    const navReserve = 84; // bottom nav clearance
    let top = r.bottom + 6;
    if (top + bh > vh - navReserve) {
      // flip above
      top = r.top - 6 - bh;
      if (top < 8) top = 8;
    }
    let left = r.left + r.width / 2 - bw / 2;
    if (left < 8) left = 8;
    if (left + bw > vw - 8) left = vw - bw - 8;
    bubble.style.top = `${Math.max(8, top)}px`;
    bubble.style.left = `${left}px`;
  }
  // Reposition on scroll/resize while open.
  window.addEventListener('scroll', () => { if (bubbleOwner) positionTip(bubbleOwner); }, true);
  window.addEventListener('resize', () => { if (bubbleOwner) positionTip(bubbleOwner); });

  // Each anchor stores its raw template + a `ctx()` function to compute live values.
  function bindTip(anchor, getZh, getEn) {
    let armed = false;
    function open() {
      showTip(anchor, getZh(), getEn());
      armed = true;
    }
    function close() { hideTip(); armed = false; }
    // Toggle on click/tap (toggletip behaviour for touch).
    anchor.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
      if (e.target.closest('input, button, a')) return;
      e.stopPropagation();
      if (armed && bubbleOwner === anchor) close();
      else open();
    });
    // Desktop: hover/focus
    anchor.addEventListener('mouseenter', () => { if (!armed) open(); });
    anchor.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => { if (bubbleOwner === anchor) close(); });
    anchor.addEventListener('focusin', () => open());
    anchor.addEventListener('focusout', () => { if (bubbleOwner === anchor) close(); });
  }
  // Global outside-tap dismiss
  document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    if (!bubbleOwner) return;
    if (bubbleOwner.contains(e.target)) return;
    hideTip();
  });

  /* ---------- Field builders ---------- */
  function fieldRow(parent, opts) {
    // opts: {nameZh, nameEn, sym, descZh, descEn, control, dynamic?}
    const row = document.createElement('div');
    row.className = 'label tip-anchor';
    row.tabIndex = 0;
    row.innerHTML = `
      <span class="zh">${opts.nameZh}</span>
      <span class="en">${opts.nameEn} <span class="sym notation">${notation(opts.sym)}</span></span>
    `;
    parent.appendChild(row);
    parent.appendChild(opts.control);
    bindTip(
      row,
      () => interp(opts.descZh, lastCtx()),
      () => interp(opts.descEn, lastCtx())
    );
    return row;
  }

  function makeInput(id, value, min, max, placeholder) {
    const w = document.createElement('div');
    w.className = 'input-wrap';
    const input = document.createElement('input');
    input.type = 'text';
    input.inputMode = 'numeric';
    input.id = id;
    input.value = value == null ? '' : String(value);
    input.placeholder = placeholder == null ? '' : String(placeholder);
    input.addEventListener('input', () => {
      input.value = input.value.replace(/[^0-9]/g, '');
      onChangeThrottled();
    });
    const s = document.createElement('div'); s.className = 'stepper';
    const up = document.createElement('button'); up.textContent = '▲'; up.type = 'button';
    const dn = document.createElement('button'); dn.textContent = '▼'; dn.type = 'button';
    function bump(delta) {
      let v = parseInt(input.value || (placeholder ?? '0'), 10);
      if (!Number.isFinite(v)) v = parseInt(placeholder ?? '0', 10) || 0;
      v += delta;
      if (max != null && v > max) v = max; if (min != null && v < min) v = min;
      input.value = String(v); onChange();
    }
    up.addEventListener('click', () => bump(+1));
    dn.addEventListener('click', () => bump(-1));
    s.appendChild(up); s.appendChild(dn);
    w.appendChild(input); w.appendChild(s);
    return w;
  }
  function makeOutput(id) {
    const o = document.createElement('div'); o.className = 'output-wrap'; o.id = id; return o;
  }

  /* ---------- Dashboard mount ---------- */
  let mounted = false;
  function mount() {
    if (mounted) return;
    mounted = true;

    // Section 1
    const s1 = $('#s1');
    s1.innerHTML = '';
    fieldRow(s1, {
      nameZh: '人數', nameEn: 'Number of Players', sym: '(n)',
      descZh: '參賽人數（至少為4且必須是正整數）',
      descEn: 'Total Number of Players (at least 4 and must be positive integer)',
      control: makeInput('inN', DEFAULTS.n, 4, 5001, DEFAULTS.n),
    });
    fieldRow(s1, {
      nameZh: '頂層選手數目', nameEn: 'Placements at the top', sym: '(p)',
      descZh: '頂層需準確地決出名次的人數（至多等於n且必須是正整數）',
      descEn: 'Accurate Ranks to determine (at most equals to n and must be positive integer)',
      control: makeInput('inP', DEFAULTS.p, 1, 5001, DEFAULTS.p),
    });
    fieldRow(s1, {
      nameZh: '積分層距離', nameEn: 'Score Group Distance', sym: '(d)',
      descZh: '自尾二輪開始避免頂層選手遇上積分層距離達d（至少為2且必須是正整數）的對手',
      descEn: 'Score Group Distance (at least 2 and must be positive integer) of the opponents against whom the top p players not to play starting from the second last round',
      control: makeInput('inD', DEFAULTS.d, 2, 9999, DEFAULTS.d),
    });

    // Section 2 (outputs only)
    const s2 = $('#s2'); s2.innerHTML = '';
    fieldRow(s2, {
      nameZh: '輪數', nameEn: 'Rounds', sym: '(Rmin - Rmax)',
      descZh: '準確地決出首<p>名選手所需的最少輪數及建議的最多輪數而超過此數目的輪數將屬多餘',
      descEn: 'Minimum number of rounds required to accurately determine top <p> placements and Maximum number of rounds recommended that more rounds beyond the number are redundant',
      control: makeOutput('outR'),
    });
    fieldRow(s2, {
      nameZh: '淘汰賽輪數', nameEn: 'Elimination Rounds', sym: '(ERmin - ERmax)',
      descZh: '在對應的最少及最多輪數下，建議附加的淘汰賽輪數',
      descEn: 'Suggested numbers of elimination rounds that go beyond the Swiss rounds for the respective minimum and maximum rounds',
      control: makeOutput('outER'),
    });
    fieldRow(s2, {

  /* ---------- Live context (single source of truth) ---------- */
  function lastCtx() {
    const n = SC.clampN($('#inN') && $('#inN').value ? $('#inN').value : DEFAULTS.n);
    const p = SC.clampP($('#inP') && $('#inP').value ? $('#inP').value : DEFAULTS.p);
    const d = SC.clampD($('#inD') && $('#inD').value ? $('#inD').value : DEFAULTS.d);
    const rRaw = $('#inR') ? $('#inR').value : '';
    const r = SC.clampR(rRaw === '' ? DEFAULTS.rPlaceholder : rRaw);
    return {
      n, p, d, r,
      pCap: SC.pCappedByN(p, n),
      rmin: SC.rMin(n, p), rmax: SC.rMax(n, p, d),
      ermin: SC.erMin(n, p), ermax: SC.erMax(n, p, d),
      lminR: SC.lmaxRmin(n, p), lmaxR: SC.lmaxRmax(n, p, d),
      nmn: SC.nMin(p, r, d), nmx: SC.nMax(p, r),
      lForN: SC.lmaxR(n, p, r),
      lNmin: SC.lmaxNmin(p, r, d), lNmax: SC.lmaxNmax(p, r),
    };
  }
  function onChange() {
    if (!mounted) return;
    const v = lastCtx();
    $('#outR').textContent = `${v.rmin} – ${v.rmax}`;
    $('#outER').textContent = `${v.ermin} – ${v.ermax}`;
    $('#outL').textContent = `${v.lminR} – ${v.lmaxR}`;
    $('#outRange').textContent = `${v.nmn} – ${v.nmx}`;
    $('#outL3').textContent = `${v.lNmin} – ${v.lForN} – ${v.lNmax}`;
    renderMatrix(v);
    // If a tooltip is open, refresh its content so live values update.
    if (bubbleOwner) {
      const ev = new Event('refresh');
      // simplest path: trigger a synthetic open on the current owner
      const owner = bubbleOwner;
      const m = owner.__refreshTip;
      if (typeof m === 'function') m();
    }
  }
  const onChangeThrottled = throttle(onChange, 100);

  /* ---------- Matrix render ---------- */
  function renderMatrix(v) {
    const wrap = $('#matrixWrap');
    const cols = SC.buildMatrix(v.p, v.d, 6144);
    const userN = v.n;
    const tbl = document.createElement('table');
    const headers = [
      { zh: '輪數', en: 'Rounds', symHTML: notation('(Rmin - Rmax)'),
        descZh: `準確地決出首<p>名選手所需的最少輪數及建議的最多輪數而超過此數目的輪數將屬多餘`,
        descEn: `Minimum number of rounds required to accurately determine top <p> placements and Maximum number of rounds recommended that more rounds beyond the number are redundant`,
        get: (c) => `${c.rmin}–${c.rmax}` },
      { zh: '淘汰賽輪數', en: 'Elimination Rounds', symHTML: notation('(ERmin - ERmax)'),
        descZh: '在對應的最少及最多輪數下，建議附加的淘汰賽輪數',
        descEn: 'Suggested numbers of elimination rounds that go beyond the Swiss rounds for the respective minimum and maximum rounds',
        get: (c) => `${c.ermin}–${c.ermax}` },
      { zh: '最多負局數', en: 'Maximum Losses', symHTML: notation('(LmaxRmin - LmaxRmax)'),
        descZh: `在對應的最少及最多輪數下，選手為擠身頂層所能容許的最多負局數`,
        descEn: `Maximum number of losses that a player could tolerate to secure a placement in the top <p> for the respective minimum and maximum rounds`,
        get: (c) => `${c.lmin}–${c.lmax}` },
      { zh: '人數範圍', en: 'Player Range', symHTML: '',
        descZh: '此列合併具有相同輪數與最多負局數的人數範圍。',
        descEn: 'This row groups player counts that share the same rounds and tolerable maximum losses.',
        get: (c) => c.nMin === c.nMax ? `${c.nMin}` : `${c.nMin}–${c.nMax}` },
    ];

    // Construct rows
    for (let r = 0; r < headers.length; r++) {
      const tr = document.createElement('tr');
      const th = document.createElement('th');
      th.className = 'head-col tip-anchor';
      th.tabIndex = 0;
      th.innerHTML = `
        <div class="head-inner">
          <span class="zh">${headers[r].zh}</span>
          <span class="en">${headers[r].en}</span>
          ${headers[r].symHTML ? `<span class="notation">${headers[r].symHTML}</span>` : ''}
        </div>`;
      // Tooltip uses live <p>/<n>/<r> interpolation.
      const hdr = headers[r];
      bindTip(
        th,
        () => interp(hdr.descZh, lastCtx()),
        () => interp(hdr.descEn, lastCtx())
      );
      tr.appendChild(th);

      cols.forEach((c) => {
        const td = document.createElement('td');
        td.textContent = hdr.get(c);
        const playerHi = userN >= c.nMin && userN <= c.nMax;
        const rangeHi = c.nMin >= v.nmn && c.nMax <= v.nmx;
        if (playerHi && rangeHi) td.classList.add('hi-both');
        else if (playerHi) td.classList.add('hi-player');
        else if (rangeHi) td.classList.add('hi-range');
        tr.appendChild(td);
      });
      tbl.appendChild(tr);
    }
    wrap.innerHTML = '';
    wrap.appendChild(tbl);
  }

    // Theme toggle (rectangular switch)

  /* ---------- Triangular orientation slider ---------- */
  // Vertex coordinates inside the 140x120 SVG viewBox.
  const TRI_VERT = {
    auto:      { x: 70,  y: 18  },
    landscape: { x: 18,  y: 104 },
    portrait:  { x: 122, y: 104 },
  };
  const KNOB_HALF = 12; // 24px knob

  function segDist(x, y, a, b) {
    const dx = b.x - a.x, dy = b.y - a.y;
    const len2 = dx * dx + dy * dy;
    let t = ((x - a.x) * dx + (y - a.y) * dy) / len2;
    if (t < 0) t = 0; else if (t > 1) t = 1;
    const px = a.x + t * dx, py = a.y + t * dy;
    return { d: Math.hypot(x - px, y - py), px, py };
  }
  function snapToPerimeter(x, y) {
    const edges = [
      [TRI_VERT.auto, TRI_VERT.landscape],
      [TRI_VERT.auto, TRI_VERT.portrait],
      [TRI_VERT.landscape, TRI_VERT.portrait],
    ];
    let best = { d: Infinity, px: TRI_VERT.auto.x, py: TRI_VERT.auto.y };
    for (const [a, b] of edges) {
      const r = segDist(x, y, a, b);
      if (r.d < best.d) best = r;
    }
    return { x: best.px, y: best.py };
  }
  function nearestVertex(x, y) {
    let best = { key: 'auto', d: Infinity };
    for (const k of ['auto', 'landscape', 'portrait']) {
      const d = Math.hypot(x - TRI_VERT[k].x, y - TRI_VERT[k].y);
      if (d < best.d) best = { key: k, d };
    }
    return best.key;
  }
  function setupOrientSlider(scope) {
    const tri = $('#orientTri', scope);
    const knob = $('#orientKnob', scope);
    if (!tri || !knob) return;

    let current = 'auto';

    function moveKnobTo(vx, vy, animate) {
      // Convert SVG-space (140x120) coords to CSS pixels using the
      // current track bounding box.
      const rect = tri.getBoundingClientRect();
      const px = (vx / 140) * rect.width  - KNOB_HALF;
      const py = (vy / 120) * rect.height - KNOB_HALF;
      tri.classList.toggle('dragging', !animate);
      knob.style.left = px + 'px';
      knob.style.top  = py + 'px';
    }
    function setActive(key) {
      current = key;
      $$('.glyph', tri).forEach((g) => g.classList.toggle('on', g.dataset.val === key));
      const legend = scope.querySelector('.legend');
      if (legend) $$('.row', legend).forEach((r) => r.classList.toggle('on', r.dataset.val === key));
    }
    function snapAndSelect(svgX, svgY) {
      const key = nearestVertex(svgX, svgY);
      const v = TRI_VERT[key];
      moveKnobTo(v.x, v.y, true);
      setActive(key);
    }
    function pointerToSvg(evt) {
      const rect = tri.getBoundingClientRect();
      const cx = (evt.clientX != null ? evt.clientX : evt.touches[0].clientX) - rect.left;
      const cy = (evt.clientY != null ? evt.clientY : evt.touches[0].clientY) - rect.top;
      return { x: (cx / rect.width) * 140, y: (cy / rect.height) * 120 };
    }

    // initial knob position (apex / Auto)
    requestAnimationFrame(() => moveKnobTo(TRI_VERT.auto.x, TRI_VERT.auto.y, true));

    // Tap a vertex glyph -> jump to it
    $$('.glyph', tri).forEach((g) =>
      g.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
        e.preventDefault();
        if (tri.classList.contains('disabled')) return;
        snapAndSelect(TRI_VERT[g.dataset.val].x, TRI_VERT[g.dataset.val].y);
      })
    );

    // Drag the knob along the perimeter
    let dragging = false;
    function onDown(e) {
      if (tri.classList.contains('disabled')) return;
      dragging = true;
      tri.setPointerCapture && e.pointerId != null && tri.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId);
      const p = pointerToSvg(e);
      const s = snapToPerimeter(p.x, p.y);
      moveKnobTo(s.x, s.y, false);
      e.preventDefault();
    }
    function onMove(e) {
      if (!dragging) return;
      const p = pointerToSvg(e);
      const s = snapToPerimeter(p.x, p.y);
      moveKnobTo(s.x, s.y, false);
      e.preventDefault();
    }
    function onUp(e) {
      if (!dragging) return;
      dragging = false;
      const p = pointerToSvg(e);
      snapAndSelect(p.x, p.y);
    }

    if (window.PointerEvent) {
      tri.addEventListener('pointerdown', onDown);
      tri.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
      tri.addEventListener('pointerup',   onUp);
      tri.addEventListener('pointercancel', onUp);
    } else {
      tri.addEventListener('mousedown', onDown);
      window.addEventListener('mousemove', onMove);
      window.addEventListener('mouseup',   onUp);
      tri.addEventListener('touchstart', onDown, { passive: false });
      tri.addEventListener('touchmove',  onMove, { passive: false });
      tri.addEventListener('touchend',   onUp);
    }
  }
})();

Changelog
MD
Changelog
All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format
follows Keep a Changelog and
this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

[1.0.8] – 2026-06-18
Fixed
Real custom fonts now ship in both builds. The placeholder TTFs
in mobile/assets/fonts/ and web/assets/fonts/ were replaced with
the actual Chiron Sung HK / Chiron Hei HK / Chiron GoRound TC / The
Peak Font Plus typefaces. Subset to the ~318 CJK + ASCII characters
the app actually uses so total font weight is ~450 KB WOFF2 / ~960
KB TTF instead of the 77 MB raw masters.
Web uses WOFF2 first with TTF fallback (Safari 11+, iOS 11+).
Mobile bundles the subset TTFs directly.
To regenerate after replacing the masters, run the pyftsubset
one-liner documented in web/css/fonts.css.
Modal close button "✕" is now perfectly centred on Safari. Switched
to flex-centering and forced font-family: 'Helvetica Neue' so the
glyph doesn't fall back to Apple Color Emoji (which has a heavy
right-anchor under Apple's fallback chain) and ends up off-centre.
"Copy Output" buttons now work in Safari over plain HTTP. Safari
blocks navigator.clipboard.writeText on non-secure origins (anything
except https:// and http://localhost) so the LAN preview at
http://192.168.x.x:port silently failed. Added a legacy fallback
using document.execCommand('copy') inside an off-screen <textarea>

references.

Tagged v1.0.8.

Summary of fixes
1️⃣ Custom fonts now load on iPhone Safari
Root cause: The TTFs in web/assets/fonts/ were 4-byte placeholders I committed during initial scaffolding ("populate them before publishing" was a TODO item, but you tested before that step).

Fix: Downloaded the real Chiron Sung HK, Chiron Hei HK, Chiron GoRound TC, and The Peak Font Plus typefaces. Subset each to just the 318 CJK + ASCII characters the app actually uses using pyftsubset. Result:

Format	Before	After
TTF total	0.016 KB (placeholders)	970 KB (subset, real glyphs)
WOFF2 total	(none)	460 KB
Web uses WOFF2 first with TTF fallback, supported on Safari 11+ / iOS 11+. Mobile uses the subset TTFs directly. The CSS comment in web/css/fonts.css documents how to regenerate after replacing the masters.

2️⃣ "Copy Output" works in Safari now
Root cause: Safari blocks navigator.clipboard.writeText on insecure origins. Your dev server is http://192.168.0.127:8765 (plain HTTP, not HTTPS, not localhost), so the API silently failed. Chrome is more permissive over LAN HTTP, so it worked there.

Fix: Added a copyToClipboard() helper that tries the modern API first (works on https:// and localhost), then falls back to the legacy document.execCommand('copy') inside an off-screen <textarea>. The fallback includes the iOS-specific focus + setSelectionRange dance that mobile Safari requires.

3️⃣ Close button "✕" now perfectly centred on Safari
Root cause: Without an explicit font family, Safari uses Apple Color Emoji as fallback for U+2715 ✕, which has a heavy right-anchor in its metrics. The cross drew flush to the right edge of the circle instead of centred.

Fix: Switched the button to flex centering (display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center) AND forced font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif so Safari uses a glyph with symmetric metrics, not Apple Color Emoji.

4️⃣ Triangular orientation slider — better visual identity
The slider is intentionally disabled on web per your spec ("(N/A on web)"). Visual updates so it reads as a slider (matching the theme switch styling) even while disabled:

Knob: white disc with 2px solid var(--primary) border + soft shadow + inset highlight — matches the round handle on the theme toggle switch.
Track: thick (6px) rounded polygon using the same --switch-track-off colour as the theme switch track; turns into the active --switch-track-on colour while being dragged (on native).
Disabled state on web: track becomes a dashed line, knob loses its shadow, cursor becomes not-allowed. Now it's visually unambiguous that it's a disabled slider, not an idle button cluster.

serve.py
PYTHON
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Local preview server with correct MIME types for fonts and modern web assets.

Python's built-in http.server reports text/plain for .woff2 / .ttf / .otf,
which Safari (more strict than Chrome) refuses to decode as a font. This
wrapper registers the right types before delegating to SimpleHTTPRequestHandler.

Usage (from inside the web/ folder):
    python serve.py            # listens on http://0.0.0.0:8765
    python serve.py 9000       # custom port
"""
import http.server
import mimetypes
import socketserver
import sys

# Register MIME types Python misses or gets wrong.
mimetypes.add_type('font/woff2', '.woff2')
mimetypes.add_type('font/woff',  '.woff')
mimetypes.add_type('font/ttf',   '.ttf')
mimetypes.add_type('font/otf',   '.otf')
mimetypes.add_type('image/svg+xml', '.svg')
mimetypes.add_type('application/javascript', '.js')
mimetypes.add_type('application/json', '.json')

PORT = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 8765
BIND = '0.0.0.0'        # force IPv4 wildcard (Python 3.14 defaults to IPv6)

class Handler(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    # Allow Safari to fetch fonts cross-origin during dev.
    def end_headers(self):
        self.send_header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*')
        self.send_header('Cache-Control', 'no-cache')
        super().end_headers()

class V4Server(socketserver.TCPServer):
    address_family = __import__('socket').AF_INET  # force IPv4
    allow_reuse_address = True

with V4Server((BIND, PORT), Handler) as httpd:
    print(f"Serving HTTP on {BIND} port {PORT} (http://{BIND}:{PORT}/) ...")
    print("Press Ctrl+C to stop.")
    try:
        httpd.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass

/*
 * @font-face declarations.
 *
 * The TTFs in assets/fonts/ are NOT committed to the repo (they are
 * licence-restricted and several megabytes each). Run the curl block
 * in assets/fonts/README.md after cloning to populate them.
 *
 * Optional: convert each TTF to WOFF2 (3-5x smaller, lossless, same
 * glyph coverage) by running web/scripts/convert-fonts-to-woff2.py.
 * The WOFF2 references below will then take precedence on browsers
 * that support them (Safari 11+, all modern Chrome/Firefox). The TTF
 * fallback covers anything older. If you do not run the converter,
 * only the TTF rule is exercised and the page still works perfectly.
 */
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Chiron Sung HK';
  src: url('../assets/fonts/ChironSungHK.woff2') format('woff2'),
       url('../assets/fonts/ChironSungHK.ttf')   format('truetype');
  font-display: swap;
  font-weight: normal;
}
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Chiron Hei HK';
  src: url('../assets/fonts/ChironHeiHK.woff2') format('woff2'),
       url('../assets/fonts/ChironHeiHK.ttf')   format('truetype');
  font-display: swap;
  font-weight: normal;
}

open
convert-fonts-to-woff2.py
PYTHON
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Optional helper — convert every .ttf in web/assets/fonts/ to .woff2.

Why?
  WOFF2 is the modern web font format. It compresses the same TTF
  payload by ~50% with NO loss of glyph data. A 24 MB TTF becomes a
  ~10 MB WOFF2 carrying every single character of the original. Every
  modern browser (Safari 11+, Chrome 36+, Firefox 39+, Edge) prefers
  it over TTF when both are listed in @font-face.

  This script does NOT subset — every glyph is preserved, so the
  legal pages on GitHub can grow new characters without re-running
  anything.

Usage (from inside web/scripts/):
    pip install fonttools brotli
    python convert-fonts-to-woff2.py

Or skip it entirely — the TTF fallback in fonts.css works fine on
its own. The conversion just trims page weight when serving over a
slow link (e.g. previewing on iPhone Safari via LAN).
"""
import os
import sys

try:
    from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
except ImportError:
    print("ERROR: fonttools not installed.")
    print("Run:  pip install fonttools brotli")
    sys.exit(1)

try:
    import brotli  # noqa: F401
except ImportError:
    print("ERROR: brotli not installed (required for WOFF2 compression).")
    print("Run:  pip install brotli")
    sys.exit(1)

here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
fonts_dir = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(here, '..', 'assets', 'fonts'))

if not os.path.isdir(fonts_dir):
    print(f"ERROR: fonts directory not found: {fonts_dir}")
    sys.exit(1)

ttfs = [f for f in os.listdir(fonts_dir) if f.lower().endswith('.ttf')]
if not ttfs:
    print(f"No .ttf files found in {fonts_dir}.")
    print("Populate them first per assets/fonts/README.md, then re-run.")
    sys.exit(0)

print(f"Converting {len(ttfs)} TTF(s) in {fonts_dir} ...")
total_in = 0
total_out = 0
for ttf in ttfs:
    src = os.path.join(fonts_dir, ttf)
    dst = os.path.join(fonts_dir, ttf[:-4] + '.woff2')
    size_in = os.path.getsize(src)
    font = TTFont(src)
    font.flavor = 'woff2'
    font.save(dst)
    size_out = os.path.getsize(dst)
    total_in += size_in
    total_out += size_out
    pct = 100 * (1 - size_out / size_in)
    print(f"  {ttf:30s} {size_in:>10,} -> {size_out:>10,} bytes  ({pct:5.1f}% smaller)")

print()
print(f"Total: {total_in:,} -> {total_out:,} bytes "
      f"({100*(1-total_out/total_in):.1f}% smaller)")
print()
print("Done. fonts.css already references the .woff2 first, so browsers")
print("that support WOFF2 will use the smaller files automatically;")
print("older browsers fall back to the .ttf.")

2. (Optional) Convert to WOFF2 for ~50% smaller payload

compressed. Modern browsers (Safari 11+, Chrome 36+, Firefox 39+) prefer

Python's built-in http.server reports text/plain for fonts, which
Safari refuses to decode. Use the project's wrapper:

python serve.py 9000
This registers the right MIME types, forces IPv4 (so iPhone can reach

Changelog
All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format
follows Keep a Changelog and
this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

[1.0.9] – 2026-06-18
Reverted
Removed font subsetting (v1.0.8) from both builds. The subsets
only contained the glyphs present in the project source at the time
of generation; remote pages (Privacy Policy, EULA, Wong system, etc.)
on GitHub can grow new glyphs at any time and the subset would not
cover them, leaving missing characters. Now the full master fonts
are referenced, and every glyph is preserved.
Changed
Fonts are no longer committed to the repo. .gitignore now
excludes every *.ttf, *.otf, *.woff, *.woff2 under
mobile/assets/fonts/ and web/assets/fonts/. Reasons:
Licence-restricted (the Chiron / Peak typefaces have their own
distribution terms).
Each TTF is 14-24 MB; together they exceed 70 MB.
They evolve independently of the app code.
Every fresh clone re-fetches them via the curl block in each
assets/fonts/README.md.
web/css/fonts.css lists WOFF2 first, TTF fallback. If WOFF2
files are present they are preferred (Safari 11+, Chrome 36+,
Firefox 39+); otherwise the TTF is used. Either path works.
Added
web/scripts/convert-fonts-to-woff2.py — optional helper that
converts every TTF in web/assets/fonts/ to WOFF2 without
subsetting. ~50 % smaller files, every glyph preserved. Run only
if you want faster loads over LAN; skip it and the TTF fallback
works fine.
web/serve.py — local-preview HTTP server that registers
correct MIME types for .ttf / .woff2 (Safari refuses to decode
fonts served as text/plain, which Python's built-in http.server
does), forces IPv4 binding (Python 3.14 defaults to IPv6-only on
Windows, which iPhones can't reach via 192.168.x.x), and adds CORS
headers.
.gitkeep files keep the empty font directories under version
control so a fresh clone has the right layout.
Documentation
Both assets/fonts/README.md files refreshed with the curl block,
the optional WOFF2 conversion step, and how to launch serve.py.
Top-level README.md web quick-start refreshed to point at the new
helper script.
[1.0.8] – 2026-06-18

the app actually uses so total font weight is ~450 KB WOFF2 / ~960
KB TTF instead of the 77 MB raw masters.
Web uses WOFF2 first with TTF fallback (Safari 11+, iOS 11+).

to flex-centering and forced font-family: 'Helvetica Neue' so the

right-anchor under Apple's fallback chain) and ends up off-centre.
"Copy Output" buttons now work in Safari over plain HTTP. Safari
blocks navigator.clipboard.writeText on non-secure origins (anything
except https:// and http://localhost) so the LAN preview at
http://192.168.x.x:port silently failed. Added a legacy fallback
using document.execCommand('copy') inside an off-screen <textarea>

Swiss Round Calculator / 瑞士制輪數計算機
MD
Swiss Round Calculator / 瑞士制輪數計算機
A fully mobile-responsive, bilingual (Traditional Chinese Hong Kong style on top of British English) calculator that computes minimum / maximum rounds of a Swiss tournament and, reversely, finds the range of player numbers a specific number of rounds supports.

This repository contains two independent deliverables:

Folder	Target	Build / Deploy
mobile/	iOS / Android app (React Native + Expo)	eas build --platform all (App Store + Google Play submission)
web/	Public website (static HTML/CSS/JS)	Upload contents of web/ to any static host (GitHub Pages, S3…)
Both versions are ad-free. The mobile app is sold via an auto-renewing annual subscription (base price 30 HKD, region-localised by RevenueCat).

Quick start
Web
Bash

cd web
# 1. Populate the fonts (one-time, ~77 MB of TTFs from GitHub):
#    see web/assets/fonts/README.md for the curl block
# 2. (Optional) shrink them to WOFF2 (~50% smaller, no glyph loss):
#    pip install fonttools brotli
#    python scripts/convert-fonts-to-woff2.py
# 3. Start the local preview (correct MIME types + IPv4 wildcard):
python serve.py            # http://0.0.0.0:8765
# or, on any host that already serves with proper MIME headers:
python3 -m http.server 8080 --bind 0.0.0.0
Then open http://<your-PC-LAN-IP>:8765 on any device on the same Wi-Fi.

Mobile
Bash

cd mobile
npm install
npx expo start
# build for stores:
eas build --platform ios
eas build --platform android
See docs/architecture-v1.md for the full architecture, data flows, upgrade hooks, and migration guide.

Features
Bilingual UI (zh-HK on top of en-GB, line-by-line, never slash-separated)
Light / Dark themes (auto + manual override, persisted)

Why Safari probably failed to render the fonts initially
You confirmed earlier that downloading http://192.168.0.127:8765/assets/fonts/ChironSungHK.ttf returned a 24.5 MB file. That means Safari CAN reach the font, but isn't using it. Two likely causes, both unrelated to subsetting:

MIME type: Python's built-in http.server returns Content-Type: application/octet-stream for .ttf. Safari (stricter than Chrome) silently refuses to use it as a font with that MIME. Fix: use the new serve.py instead:

Bash

cd web
python serve.py
It registers font/ttf correctly. Refresh Safari — fonts should appear.

Slow first paint over LAN: 24.5 MB × 4 fonts = ~100 MB to download before the page can render text. If Safari times out the font load, it falls back to system fonts. The optional WOFF2 conversion brings each font down to ~10-12 MB and load time drops dramatically without touching glyph coverage:

Bash

cd web/scripts
pip install fonttools brotli
python convert-fonts-to-woff2.py
Re-run any time you replace the masters. Future-proof against new glyphs in remote pages.

TL;DR for testing on iPhone Safari
Bash

cd /c/path/to/swiss-round-calculator/web
# (one-time, optional) shrink the full TTFs without losing any glyph:
pip install fonttools brotli
python scripts/convert-fonts-to-woff2.py
# every time you want to preview:
python serve.py
Then on iPhone Safari → http://192.168.0.127:8765. With correct MIME types and (optionally) WOFF2 compression, the custom fonts will load properly.

 * @font-face declarations.
 *
 * TTF format only — chosen so the same font files can be embedded into
 * SVG masters (app icon, splash screens) and rendered identically by
 * any SVG processor. WOFF / WOFF2 are intentionally NOT used here even
 * though they are smaller, because they require an extra conversion

 * The TTFs themselves are NOT committed to the repo (licence-restricted

  font-weight: normal;

Why TTF and not WOFF/WOFF2?
TTF is chosen deliberately so that the exact same font file can be:

Loaded by browsers via @font-face (web build).
Bundled into the React Native app via require('./X.ttf').
Embedded into SVG masters (app icon, splash screens) for pixel-perfect
rasterisation by any SVG processor (Inkscape, resvg-js, ImageMagick).
WOFF / WOFF2 are smaller but not universally recognised by SVG
processors, so using them would split the typography pipeline.

Why font-display: block?
fonts.css uses font-display: block (not swap). With swap, the
browser paints text in a fallback system font first and then "swaps" to
the custom font when it arrives — which can produce a layout shift and,
on some browsers, occasionally never swap if loading was cancelled.
block waits up to ~3 seconds for the TTF to download before painting
text at all. The trade-off: a brief delay on first paint over a slow
LAN, in exchange for guaranteed correct typography every time.

This matches the behaviour of the upstream GitHub Pages
(e.g. https://vviinncceenntt.github.io/wongssystem.html).

Serving the site locally with correct MIME types
Python's built-in http.server reports application/octet-stream for
.ttf, which Safari refuses to decode as a font. Use the project's
wrapper:

Bash

cd web
python serve.py             # http://0.0.0.0:8765
# or with a custom port:
python serve.py 9000
serve.py registers font/ttf correctly, forces IPv4 binding
(Python 3.14 defaults to IPv6-only on Windows, which iPhones on the
same Wi-Fi cannot reach via 192.168.x.x), and adds CORS headers.

Changelog
All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format

[1.0.9] – 2026-06-18
Reverted (v1.0.8 → restored full fonts)
Removed font subsetting from both builds. The subsets only
contained the glyphs present in the project source at the time of
generation; remote pages (Privacy Policy, EULA, Wong system, etc.)
on GitHub can grow new glyphs at any time and the subset would not
cover them. Now the full master TTFs are referenced and every
glyph is preserved.
Removed WOFF2 generation and web/scripts/convert-fonts-to-woff2.py.
The project intentionally standardises on TTF so the same font
file can be reused for browser @font-face, React-Native
require(), and SVG-embedded <style>@font-face</style> for the
app-icon / splash-screen generators. WOFF / WOFF2 are smaller but
not universally recognised by SVG rasterisers (resvg-js, ImageMagick,
Inkscape), and mixing formats would split the typography pipeline.
Changed
web/css/fonts.css: simplified to TTF only with
font-display: block (was swap). Reasons documented in the
file header:
Matches the upstream GitHub Pages (e.g.
https://vviinncceenntt.github.io/wongssystem.html) which also use
block.
swap was producing a flash of fallback system font that
sometimes never resolved to the custom font on slower networks.
block waits up to ~3 s for the TTF, then paints text correctly
every time.
Fonts remain committed to the repo (the user keeps them in
GitHub alongside their licence files). .gitignore no longer
excludes font files.
Added
web/serve.py — local-preview HTTP server that registers correct
MIME types for .ttf (Safari refuses to decode fonts served as
text/plain, which Python's built-in http.server does), forces
IPv4 binding (Python 3.14 defaults to IPv6-only on Windows, which
iPhones cannot reach via 192.168.x.x), and adds CORS headers.
Documentation
Both assets/fonts/README.md files refreshed with the curl block,
the rationale for TTF-only, the font-display: block choice, and
how to launch serve.py.
Top-level README.md web quick-start simplified to two commands.

[1.0.4] – 2026-06-16
Fixed
scripts/generate-assets.sh:
Locale-safe stderr truncation. Replaced the awk byte-length filter
with an LC_ALL=C invocation so Git Bash on Windows no longer prints
awk: warning: Invalid multibyte data detected when ImageMagick
emits localised (Chinese / mojibake) error strings.
Recursive remote-resource inlining. The Node inliner now follows
nested @font-face url('https://...') CSS references (Lato,
Parisienne, Cubic 11, Compact, …) — fonts are fetched once and
embedded as data:font/ttf;base64,... so resvg-js renders text in
the correct typeface instead of stacking glyphs at the origin
(which previously made "Vincent" look like a pile of letters).
Nested-SVG unwrap. When an SVG embeds another SVG via
<image href="...">, the inliner now unwraps that base-64 data
URI into a real inline <svg>…</svg> block. resvg-js does not
resolve @font-face declarations from inside a referenced image,
but does resolve them from sibling/nested <svg> elements, so the
Android-12 splash's centred app-icon now renders its "Vincent"
label and keypad correctly.
Recursion depth-cap of 4 keeps the inliner safe against cyclic
references.

Swiss Round Calculator / 瑞士制輪數計算機
A fully mobile-responsive, bilingual (Traditional Chinese Hong Kong style on top of British English) calculator that computes minimum / maximum rounds of a Swiss tournament and, reversely, finds the range of player numbers a specific number of rounds supports.

Tagged v1.0.9 (revised).

Summary
Two changes to match your setup
What	From	To
Font format references	TTF + WOFF2 (with optional WOFF2 conversion script)	TTF only
font-display value	swap	block
What font-display: block does
The browser hides the text completely (renders blank space) for up to ~3 seconds while waiting for the TTF to download. If the font arrives in time, text paints with the correct typeface; if not, it falls back to the system font. Crucially, once the TTF eventually downloads, the text re-renders with the custom font — and it stays that way for the rest of the session. No more "sometimes I see Chiron, sometimes I see fallback" inconsistency.

The trade-off is a brief blank moment on first paint over slow networks, but you've explicitly said you prefer that over inconsistent rendering — same call as your GitHub Pages source.

TTF-only rationale (now in the README header)
Same TTF file feeds three different consumers:

Browser @font-face (the web build).
React-Native require() (mobile bundle).
Embedded inside SVG masters via <style>@font-face{src:url(...ttf)}</style> (app icon, splash screens — see generate-assets.sh).
WOFF/WOFF2 are smaller for the browser path but resvg-js, ImageMagick, and Inkscape don't all recognise them when embedded in SVG. Standardising on TTF keeps every part of the pipeline using the same exact bytes.

Removed / restored
Removed: web/scripts/convert-fonts-to-woff2.py (no longer needed)
Removed: web/scripts/ directory (now empty)
Restored: .gitignore no longer excludes font files — your repo will continue tracking the TTFs alongside their licence files as you have it
Removed: .gitkeep placeholders (font dirs now hold the real TTFs in your setup)
Kept
web/serve.py — still needed for iPhone Safari preview because Python's built-in http.server reports TTFs as application/octet-stream (Safari refuses) and binds to IPv6-only on Python 3.14 (iPhones can't reach via 192.168.x.x).

On launch, fetch each remote page in the background.
